questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Will let you see well to both sides.
Will prevent you from turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will let you see well to both sides.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers. Reflective materials help even more.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:
questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash, keep you comfortable, and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. If vehicles are on both sides, the center lane position is usually safest.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test both brakes to make sure each one activates the brake lights.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: Using both brakes:

options.text: Should be done every time you stop.
Should only be done in emergencies.
Should only be done on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done every time you stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle for safety before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at the higher speed, which is even more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body faster. Your body removes one drink per hour on average. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after one hour passes.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes with controlled pressure at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Limit how much you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest, even if you don't feel tired. Most experienced riders limit themselves to six hours of riding per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire faster, so dress to protect yourself from the elements.

questions.question: What is the benefit of reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing?

options.text: They should only be worn at night.
They help other drivers see you.
They do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing increases your chances of being seen by other drivers.

questions.question: What should riders know about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: They do not exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What should be your main concern when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much protection it offers.
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT standards.

questions.question: What color and letters are service signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what is important?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: You must watch the road ahead and behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: When cars merge from an entrance ramp, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Never assume the drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume drivers see you. Give them plenty of space. Move to another lane if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist avoid doing?

options.text: Keep knees against the gas tank while riding.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests while riding.
Raise the handlebars so hands are above the elbows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the handlebars so hands are above the elbows.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands at or below your elbow level. This gives you better control when steering. Keep your feet on the footrests and knees against the gas tank for better balance when turning.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the vehicle to move.
Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle and proceed slowly. Slow down and be ready to stop when approaching an emergency scene.
